title: Research: elementary-abelian diagonal minimum is the non-identity count (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For every rank `k≥2`, every finite register count `n`, and every diagonal in `F₂[(C₂)^k]`, a legal non-identity rank-one update `I+(g-1)xy^T` (`y^T x=1`) has exact paid-call minimum **`t`**, the number of non-identity diagonal entries. Identity coordinates are restored dirty spectators and do not lower that minimum.

The obstruction is graded image rank. Writing `R=F₂[z₁,…,z_k]/(z₁²,…,z_k²)` and `m=(z₁,…,z_k)`, a product of `L` paid factors satisfies `dim im π(P-I) ≤ L` in `m/m²`. On a diagonal the `t` vectors `e_i ⊗ π(h_i-1)` are linearly independent, including when several entries share an image. Coordinate calls `I+(h_i-1)e_i e_i^T` attain `t`.

This is not the chain-ring theorem of merged [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513). That proof assumes `R=F₂[z]/(z^q)` and one-dimensional socles of principal ideals. For `k≥2`, `dim m/m²=k` and `(z₁)` is incomparable with `(z₂)`. The one-column witness `U=(z₁,z₂)^T` in #2513 is cited there as not a shorter circuit. Labels outside a single `C₂` stay inside the same span, so they cannot beat `t`. The `q=2` chain-ring case is the excluded rank `k=1`. The `C₄` involution `1+z²` lies in `1+m²`, so this count does not apply there and the four-involution census is not recomputed.

The length-2 enumerations (129600 products at `(k,n)=(2,4)`, 38416 at `(3,3)`) are controls. **No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`. No supplier and no shorter cyclic 2-power circuit.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/elementary-abelian-diagonal-minimum/`
- Tip: `cafc1f602e85b8142e36d5b3adf40187dfb0067a`
- Base: `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`
- Scope: **refined** — graded image minimum for elementary abelian diagonals, outside the chain-ring hypothesis

Closest prior: [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513). PROOF sequence overlap ≈0.026, token Jaccard ≈0.27, exact shared nonempty lines 0. A pin search finds `F₂[x,y]/(x²,y²)` only in that predecessor, and only as a non-circuit witness.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/elementary-abelian-diagonal-minimum/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/elementary-abelian-diagonal-minimum/test_verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/elementary-abelian-diagonal-minimum
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_ELEMENTARY_ABELIAN_DIAGONAL_MINIMUM
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/elementary-abelian-diagonal-minimum outcome=completed
```

`test_verify.py` runs 8 tests, including a dictionary multiplier that does not call the verifier's product routine. Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Credit

Credit [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513) (`research/bit-cyclic-root-barrier`) for the chain-ring diagonal theorem and the explicit non-chain socle witness, and Cinna Davis for the C4 root-lift credited there. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Does a nonabelian group algebra of order at most 16 admit a legal diagonal word shorter than its non-identity count in this rank-one model? The graded bound uses commutativity and a nonzero image in `m/m²`. A first step is to list which non-identity elements lie in `1+m²` before searching.
2. Native frame, hosting, and precision bills remain unpriced.
3. Do not rerun the cyclic 2-power socle census.
